Title: ‘Relationship Goals’ Soundtrack Album Details – Film Music Reporter
Chunks: 0,1
Lakeshore Records will release a soundtrack album for the romantic comedy **Relationship Goals**. The album features the film’s original score composed by **Dara Taylo**r(_Ironheart_, _Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar_, _The Invitation, Strays, Straw,_ _The Tender Bar_, _Meet Me Next Christmas_,_Echo Boomers_, _The Noel Diary_). The soundtrack will be released digitally tomorrow, February 6 and will be available to stream/download on Amazon and any other major digital music services. Also listen to the composer’s title track below. As previously reported, KTR Records has released the original song _Complicated_ performed by lead actors Kelly Rowland & Cliff “Method Man” Smith as a separate digital single last week. _Relationship Goals_ is directed by Linda Mendoza and also stars Robin Thede, Annie Gonzalez, Dennis Haysbert and Matt Walsh. The movie follows a TV producer Leah Caldwell who aims to become the first woman running New York’s top morning show, when her ex swoops in to compete for the same role and claims to be changed by the titular New York Times bestselling book. The comedy just premiered yesterday and is now available to stream exclusively on Prime Video.

## by Sheldon Rocha Leal
11 min read
May 23, 2022
Press enter or click to view image in full size
The juncture at which Art and Music meet I find to be a fascinating space. In my last article, I highlighted the contributions made by some of the 20th century’s greatest fine artists to the music industry in the guise of Album cover design. In this article, I’m taking the topic one step further. One of my favourite topics to read about is the life and times of successful people. I have, therefore, read many biographies and autobiographies, but as a music person, many of these have been about music people (executives, managers, musicians and recording artists).
What motivates me to read these books is the fact that I like knowing what makes successful people “tick”. With regards to famous people, I want to get into the anatomy of how these people have managed to capture the prevailing zeitgeist in what they do and the content they create. By being enlightened about the context and motivation behind what people do, I hope to apply some of these concepts in my own life and practice. Having read many music biographies, and most recently a David Bowie one, I have started picking up a common denominator amongst some of these famous recording artists. The commonality is the fact that many started off their careers studying Art at Art School. The list of famous Rock stars that are art school alumni is long and I have been pondering about the motivation behind their decision to pursue art studies as opposed to what they would ultimately succeed at, music.
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Creatives are often proficient in various arts disciplines.

## by Sheldon Rocha Leal
I have opinions about what these motivations could be. Firstly, many students who pursue a specific artistic discipline at school opt to embark on a different artistic journey post-school either because they are burnt out or because they want to try something new. Secondly, formal music education is very expensive, therefore, precluding many hopefuls from immersing themselves in this type of academic pursuit, art, therefore, affords them a creative outlet. Thirdly, many creatively inclined people will be able to express themselves in different artistic disciplines, they might therefore opt for one discipline initially and change course later or explore them simultaneously. Fourthly, many music programmes have been terminated around the world, therefore, placing this type of education out of the reach of many. Lastly, the type of music education promoted at many institutions is out of touch with what is happening in the music industry and is, therefore, not perceived as relevant or interesting for a prospective student. In the end, I guess people’s reasons for making the decision to pursue an artistic path are as varied as the people themselves.
But without further ado, let me revert back to the focus of this article: 5 art school alumni, who studied art instead of music in their scholarly pursuits. All five music stars majored in art either at high school or tertiary level. The 5 individuals selected are, David Bowie, Freddie Mercury, John Lennon, Eric Clapton and Florence Walsh. These “Rock Stars” were and are still considered major influences in their respective area of music, which makes the fact that they didn’t study music at school puzzling and the point from which I depart on this article…

## by Sheldon Rocha Leal
### David Bowie
Press enter or click to view image in full size
David Bowie was known as the Chameleon of Pop because he changed his look for many times.
David Bowie, or “The Think White Duke”, Ziggy Stardust, Aladdin Sane, The Blind Prophet, Pierrot or The Chameleon of Pop as he has variously been known, was born on the 8th of January 1947. That happens to also be the same day on which another icon was born, Elvis Presley, albeit 12 years earlier (1935). He was born in London, England and his parents were humble workers (mother a waitress, father a promotions officer at a charity). He showed signs of giftedness from as early as 6 years, with teachers saying he was very focused, but prone to brawling (probably because he was bored).
At school, his teachers felt that he was an average singer, but exhibited other creative talents, such as dance. His dad, one of his biggest supporters, exposed him to Rock ‘n Roll music. It is said that when Bowie heard “Tutti Frutti” by Little Richard for the first time he expressed that he had heard God. In his high school years, he attended Bromley Technical High School (now known as Ravens Wood School), which specialises in the arts. At the school, he studied art, music and design including layout and typesetting. Whilst there he studied Saxophone and added to his repertoire of instruments including Ukulele, Bass Guitar, Guitar and Piano.
Press enter or click to view image in full size
The “1. Outside” album cover was based on an artwork created by David Bowie titled “DHead XLVI”.

## by Sheldon Rocha Leal
### David Bowie
Bowie became one of the most significant figures in Popular Music History. He released 26 studio albums and 128 singles, shipped over 140million records worldwide and won 6 Grammy and 4 Brit Awards. His talents were, however, not limited to music alone. He acted in 37 movies, produced 3, and dabbled in art, amassing an impressive art collection. When he passed away in 2016 his art collection was auctioned off for $32.9million and included works by Basquiat, Damien Hirst, Marcel Duchamp and Rubens. The collection did not include any of his own paintings or sculptures. One of his pieces was used as the cover of the “1. Outside” album (his 20th studio album) released in 1995. The artwork titled “DHead XLVI” was auctioned off in 2021 for $87,000.

## by Sheldon Rocha Leal
### Freddie Mercury
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Freddie Mercury was the lead singer of the legendary Queen band.
The lead singer of the iconic Rock band Queen was born in Zanzibar on the 5th of September 1946. His parents were from Western India and his father worked for the British Colonial Office. As a result, Freddie moved around a lot as a child, living in Zanzibar, India and eventually U.K. Whilst attending St Peter’s School in Bombay, a British type boarding school, he formed his first band, “The Hectics”, who covered Rock ‘n Roll songs by artists such as Cliff Richard and Little Richard (not related). When the family eventually moved to England, fleeing a revolution in Zanzibar, he attended Ealing Art College, aged 18. The College was established as a further education institution in the 1960s focusing on Fashion, Graphic, Industrial Design, Photography and Fine Arts education.

Remember me for faster sign in
Freddie Mercury graduated from the institution in 1969 with a Diploma in Graphic Art and Design. He was, however, intent on pursuing his passion for music and post his studies joined various bands, eventually teaming up with Brian May and Roger Taylor in 1970 to form a band initially known as Smile. John Deacon subsequently joined the band and Queen was born. The band went on to become one of the most significant and influential Rock bands in history, shipping over 300million records in just over 2 decades. “Bohemian Rhapsody”, released in 1975 is considered one of the most significant songs in Popular music history. The band released 15 studio albums, and 72 singles and were inducted into the Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame (2001), Hollywood Walk of Fame (2002) and Freddie was inducted into the Songwriter’s Hall of Fame (2003) in a solo capacity. “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “We Will Rock Rock” have both been inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Queen Crest was designed by Freddie Mercury and was featured on various Queen projects, including album covers.
Although a very successful rock star, possibly because of his Art roots, he had a very strong visual aesthetic, which was evident in his stage shows, music videos and album covers. He famously designed the band’s logo, known as “Queen Crest”, which features the zodiac signs of all 4 band members: Leo (Roger Taylor and John Deacon), Cancer (Brian May) and Virgo (Freddie Mercury). The crest featured prominently on the covers of “A Night At The Opera” (1975), “A Day At The Races” (1976) and “Greatest Hits II” (1991).

## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### John Lennon
Press enter or click to view image in full size
John Lennon has a prolific career as a musician, but he was also an artist.
John Lennon was born in Liverpool, England on the 9th of October 1940 and went on to become the founding member of the most successful band in music history, The Beatles. He was raised by his mom (Julia), stepfather and eventually his aunt (Mimi). Julia bought John his first guitar and exposed him to Rock ‘n Roll music, particularly records by Elvis Presley and Fats Domino. Besides his aptitude for music, he also displayed an inclination for art and communicated to his aunt that he would one day be famous.
John Lennon failed his O-Levels and was later accepted at The Liverpool College of Art (a higher education institution), established in 1825 as the Liverpool Mechanics’ School of Art Institute. Lennon was eventually kicked out of the school before his final year but had been informally dabbling in music and doing gigs whilst studying. His aunt Mimi was opposed to the people with whom he was interacting and did not support his music endeavours. This did not, however, prevent him from pursuing his first love, Music. Eventually, the Beatles were formed and went on to become the biggest selling band of all time, shipping over 500million records worldwide. Additionally, they attained 15 No1 albums in the UK, 19 in the USA, 17 No1 singles in the U.K. and 20 in the USA. This excludes John Lennon’s solo output, which includes an additional 3 U.K./USA No1 albums and 3 No1 U.K. singles. Lennon is undoubtedly one of the most influential musicians of all time.
Press enter or click to view image in full size
This is one of John Lennon’s famous lithographs. This is a self-portrait that was also used as the album cover of his “Imagine” documentary project.

## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### John Lennon
Besides being a famous recording artist Lennon was also impactful in the art world. After meeting Yoko Ono, his second wife, who is a performance artist, he got more involved in arts endeavours, famously funding and bankrolling many of her exhibitions. He also started creating his own art at this time, exhibiting from 1968 onward. In 1970 Lennon exhibited at Eugene Schuster’s London Arts Gallery. His lithographs are probably the works for which he is most famous. Over 3,000 prints were made of the lithographs and 300 complete sets of 14 lithographs were packaged in white leather bags featuring the words “Bag One” embossed on the bags. Today these lithographs sell for between £2,000 and £16,000 apiece. Lennon also exhibited with his wife and was known to make art movies, for example “Erection” (1971) a movie edited on 16mm film.

## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### Eric Clapton
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Eric Clapton is the only artist in history to be inducted into the Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame three times.
The Bluesman was born on 30 March 1945 in Surrey, England. He was brought up by his grandparents, who he was led to believe were his parents, whilst his sister was in actual fact his biological mother. Patricia (his mother) was 16 years old when he was born. He attended Hollyfield School in Surbiton and after completing his secondary schooling enrolled at the Kingston College of Art (now known as Kingston University) to study art. Clapton was expelled from the institution after his first year because his focus was more on his music than his art.
Eric Clapton has gone on to become one of the most prolific musicians in music history, performing as part of various successful acts. These include Cream, The Yardbirds, John Mayall & The Bluesbreakers, Blind Faith, Delaney and Bonnie and Friends and Derek & The Dominoes. This excludes the immense success he later attained as a solo artist. The 17 time Grammy Award winner has been inducted into the Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame on 3 different occasions, as a solo artist, a member of Cream and The Yardbirds (the most by any artist). His musical output is extraordinary with 24 solo and 23 band albums released in a 60-year career.
Press enter or click to view image in full size
The above are some of the album covers on which Eric Clapton has worked for his solo released: “From The Cradle” (1994) (top left); “Me and Mr Johnson” (2004) (top right); “Pilgrim” (1998) (middle left); “Old Sock” (2013) (bottom right); “The Breeze: An Appreciation of JJ Cale” (2014) (bottom left).

## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### Eric Clapton
“Slow Hand”, as he is sometimes known, utilising his artistic eye, has taken an active role in the design and packaging of all his albums over the years. He usually works closely with the photographers, artists and designers to bring his aesthetic visions to life. The cover of his collaborative album “The Breeze: An Appreciation of JJ Cale” (2014) was conceptualised by Clapton. The “Old Sock” (2013) cover was based on selfies taken by Eric Clapton and “Me & Mr Johnson” (2004) on photographs taken by the legend. The “Pilgrim” (1998) cover and packaging were conceptualised by Eric Clapton, whilst the typeface on the cover of “From The Cradle” (1994) was designed by the musician. Eric Clapton is also an avid art collector, famously selling one of his Gerhard Richter artworks at an auction in 2012 for $34million and another in 2016 for $20million. These works were sold at a massive profit considering he purchased 3 of them in 2001 for $3.4million, eventually selling them for over $74million.

## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### Florence Welch
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Florence Welch is the lead singer of Florence+The Machine.
Florence was born in Camberwell, London on 28 August 1986. Her mother is a Professor of Renaissance studies and her father is an advertising executive. She displayed an early interest in music, a talent encouraged by her grandmother. She received her secondary school education at Alleyn’s School in South East London, excelling academically. After leaving school she enrolled at Camberwell College of Arts, a fine art tertiary institution in the area in which she was born. She eventually dropped out of the college to focus on her music career, which had always been her overriding passion.
In 2006 she formed the band Florence+The Machine, who have to date released 5 studio albums, three of which have peaked at No1 in the U.K. and 1 in the USA. The band has shipped over 20million records worldwide and released over 20 singles, attracting mass critical acclaim. Florence+The Machine has won various awards including the Brit Award and Florence Welch has won the Ivor Novello award for songwriting in her personal capacity. Welch is well known for her distinctive stage image and fashion sense. The band’s music videos are stylised and the albums follow a similar design aesthetic. This could have possibly derived from her art school training, as well as her passion for literature.
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Florence Welch was the art director on her band’s first studio album release, “Lungs” (2009).

## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### Florence Welch
Art and Florence+The Machine are synonymous. A different art movement has inspired each album. The first album, “Lungs” (2009), had a distinctly Victorian feel and the singer even art directed the project. The 2nd album, “Ceremonials” (2011), is more Art Deco-inspired in design, whilst the image and look of the 3rd album, “How Big, How Blue, How Beautiful” (2015), followed a 1960s aesthetic. The 4th studio album, “High As Hope” (2018) contained a drawing by the singer and the 5th album “Dance Fever” (2022), has a distinctive Pre-Raphaelite influence. Welch works closely with an art team for each one of her albums and has consistently used Tom Beard as a photographer.
It is interesting to note that all of the above musicians, have maintained a close relationship with their art roots and it seems that the older they get the more they dabble in this sphere. Art is an essential component of music, it is the trigger that entices an audience to click on the music. As they say “we eat with our eyes first” and art most certainly is the precursor to the final music product. I have many times bought an album merely because I was intrigued by the album cover, curious to determine if the images related to the music, sparking off my musical imagination. My belief has always been that the arts are strongest when we (as creators) stand together. Seeing the different creative disciplines converge makes me really happy, hence the motivation to write this article. The great thing is that young musical artists are increasingly displaying an understanding of the importance of art as part of their final product and this feature is playing a more prominent in the music-making process and life-cycle.

This Friday is the birthday of Robyn Hitchcock, an influential musician who was a member of the Soft Boys in the 1970s and who continues a vibrant career as a solo artist. Hitchcock is based in Nashville nowadays, but he was born in England and got his start in music after joining a band while he was attending art school in London.
It turns out Hitchcock is among legions of musicians who at one time in their lives attended art school at four-year universities or at smaller institutions dedicated to the arts. Whether they graduated or not, many musicians spent time studying the visual arts — photography, graphic design, filmmaking, painting, sculpture, illustration. Many musicians, like Florence Welch or Joe Strummer, attended art school and got into their music careers later. Meanwhile, there are several bands we know and love who formed when the members met while students at art school; for example, Chuck D and Flavor Flav of Public Enemy met one another while attending Adelphi University, where Chuck D studied graphic design.

Freddie Mercury was the lead singer of the legendary Queen band.
The lead singer of the iconic Rock band Queen was born in Zanzibar on the 5th of September 1946. His parents were from Western India and his father worked for the British Colonial Office. As a result, Freddie moved around a lot as a child, living in Zanzibar, India and eventually U.K. Whilst attending St Peter’s School in Bombay, a British type boarding school, he formed his first band, “The Hectics”, who covered Rock ‘n Roll songs by artists such as Cliff Richard and Little Richard (not related). When the family eventually moved to England, fleeing a revolution in Zanzibar, he attended Ealing Art College, aged 18. The College was established as a further education institution in the 1960s focusing on Fashion, Graphic, Industrial Design, Photography and Fine Arts education.

Freddie Mercury graduated from the institution in 1969 with a Diploma in Graphic Art and Design. He was, however, intent on pursuing his passion for music and post his studies joined various bands, eventually teaming up with Brian May and Roger Taylor in 1970 to form a band initially known as Smile. John Deacon subsequently joined the band and Queen was born. The band went on to become one of the most significant and influential Rock bands in history, shipping over 300million records in just over 2 decades. “Bohemian Rhapsody”, released in 1975 is considered one of the most significant songs in Popular music history. The band released 15 studio albums, and 72 singles and were inducted into the Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame (2001), Hollywood Walk of Fame (2002) and Freddie was inducted into the Songwriter’s Hall of Fame (2003) in a solo capacity. “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “We Will Rock Rock” have both been inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.

Queen Crest was designed by Freddie Mercury and was featured on various Queen projects, including album covers.
Although a very successful rock star, possibly because of his Art roots, he had a very strong visual aesthetic, which was evident in his stage shows, music videos and album covers. He famously designed the band’s logo, known as “Queen Crest”, which features the zodiac signs of all 4 band members: Leo (Roger Taylor and John Deacon), Cancer (Brian May) and Virgo (Freddie Mercury). The crest featured prominently on the covers of “A Night At The Opera” (1975), “A Day At The Races” (1976) and “Greatest Hits II” (1991).

### John Lennon
Press enter or click to view image in full size
John Lennon has a prolific career as a musician, but he was also an artist.
John Lennon was born in Liverpool, England on the 9th of October 1940 and went on to become the founding member of the most successful band in music history, The Beatles. He was raised by his mom (Julia), stepfather and eventually his aunt (Mimi). Julia bought John his first guitar and exposed him to Rock ‘n Roll music, particularly records by Elvis Presley and Fats Domino. Besides his aptitude for music, he also displayed an inclination for art and communicated to his aunt that he would one day be famous.
John Lennon failed his O-Levels and was later accepted at The Liverpool College of Art (a higher education institution), established in 1825 as the Liverpool Mechanics’ School of Art Institute. Lennon was eventually kicked out of the school before his final year but had been informally dabbling in music and doing gigs whilst studying. His aunt Mimi was opposed to the people with whom he was interacting and did not support his music endeavours. This did not, however, prevent him from pursuing his first love, Music. Eventually, the Beatles were formed and went on to become the biggest selling band of all time, shipping over 500million records worldwide. Additionally, they attained 15 No1 albums in the UK, 19 in the USA, 17 No1 singles in the U.K. and 20 in the USA. This excludes John Lennon’s solo output, which includes an additional 3 U.K./USA No1 albums and 3 No1 U.K. singles. Lennon is undoubtedly one of the most influential musicians of all time.

### John Lennon
Besides being a famous recording artist Lennon was also impactful in the art world. After meeting Yoko Ono, his second wife, who is a performance artist, he got more involved in arts endeavours, famously funding and bankrolling many of her exhibitions. He also started creating his own art at this time, exhibiting from 1968 onward. In 1970 Lennon exhibited at Eugene Schuster’s London Arts Gallery. His lithographs are probably the works for which he is most famous. Over 3,000 prints were made of the lithographs and 300 complete sets of 14 lithographs were packaged in white leather bags featuring the words “Bag One” embossed on the bags. Today these lithographs sell for between £2,000 and £16,000 apiece. Lennon also exhibited with his wife and was known to make art movies, for example “Erection” (1971) a movie edited on 16mm film.

### Eric Clapton
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Eric Clapton is the only artist in history to be inducted into the Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame three times.
The Bluesman was born on 30 March 1945 in Surrey, England. He was brought up by his grandparents, who he was led to believe were his parents, whilst his sister was in actual fact his biological mother. Patricia (his mother) was 16 years old when he was born. He attended Hollyfield School in Surbiton and after completing his secondary schooling enrolled at the Kingston College of Art (now known as Kingston University) to study art. Clapton was expelled from the institution after his first year because his focus was more on his music than his art.
Eric Clapton has gone on to become one of the most prolific musicians in music history, performing as part of various successful acts. These include Cream, The Yardbirds, John Mayall & The Bluesbreakers, Blind Faith, Delaney and Bonnie and Friends and Derek & The Dominoes. This excludes the immense success he later attained as a solo artist. The 17 time Grammy Award winner has been inducted into the Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame on 3 different occasions, as a solo artist, a member of Cream and The Yardbirds (the most by any artist). His musical output is extraordinary with 24 solo and 23 band albums released in a 60-year career.

### Eric Clapton
“Slow Hand”, as he is sometimes known, utilising his artistic eye, has taken an active role in the design and packaging of all his albums over the years. He usually works closely with the photographers, artists and designers to bring his aesthetic visions to life. The cover of his collaborative album “The Breeze: An Appreciation of JJ Cale” (2014) was conceptualised by Clapton. The “Old Sock” (2013) cover was based on selfies taken by Eric Clapton and “Me & Mr Johnson” (2004) on photographs taken by the legend. The “Pilgrim” (1998) cover and packaging were conceptualised by Eric Clapton, whilst the typeface on the cover of “From The Cradle” (1994) was designed by the musician. Eric Clapton is also an avid art collector, famously selling one of his Gerhard Richter artworks at an auction in 2012 for $34million and another in 2016 for $20million. These works were sold at a massive profit considering he purchased 3 of them in 2001 for $3.4million, eventually selling them for over $74million.

### Florence Welch
Press enter or click to view image in full size
Florence Welch is the lead singer of Florence+The Machine.
Florence was born in Camberwell, London on 28 August 1986. Her mother is a Professor of Renaissance studies and her father is an advertising executive. She displayed an early interest in music, a talent encouraged by her grandmother. She received her secondary school education at Alleyn’s School in South East London, excelling academically. After leaving school she enrolled at Camberwell College of Arts, a fine art tertiary institution in the area in which she was born. She eventually dropped out of the college to focus on her music career, which had always been her overriding passion.
In 2006 she formed the band Florence+The Machine, who have to date released 5 studio albums, three of which have peaked at No1 in the U.K. and 1 in the USA. The band has shipped over 20million records worldwide and released over 20 singles, attracting mass critical acclaim. Florence+The Machine has won various awards including the Brit Award and Florence Welch has won the Ivor Novello award for songwriting in her personal capacity. Welch is well known for her distinctive stage image and fashion sense. The band’s music videos are stylised and the albums follow a similar design aesthetic. This could have possibly derived from her art school training, as well as her passion for literature.

Florence Welch was the art director on her band’s first studio album release, “Lungs” (2009).
texts.11:
## Get Sheldon Rocha Leal, PhD’s stories in your inbox
### Florence Welch
Art and Florence+The Machine are synonymous. A different art movement has inspired each album. The first album, “Lungs” (2009), had a distinctly Victorian feel and the singer even art directed the project. The 2nd album, “Ceremonials” (2011), is more Art Deco-inspired in design, whilst the image and look of the 3rd album, “How Big, How Blue, How Beautiful” (2015), followed a 1960s aesthetic. The 4th studio album, “High As Hope” (2018) contained a drawing by the singer and the 5th album “Dance Fever” (2022), has a distinctive Pre-Raphaelite influence. Welch works closely with an art team for each one of her albums and has consistently used Tom Beard as a photographer.
It is interesting to note that all of the above musicians, have maintained a close relationship with their art roots and it seems that the older they get the more they dabble in this sphere. Art is an essential component of music, it is the trigger that entices an audience to click on the music. As they say “we eat with our eyes first” and art most certainly is the precursor to the final music product. I have many times bought an album merely because I was intrigued by the album cover, curious to determine if the images related to the music, sparking off my musical imagination. My belief has always been that the arts are strongest when we (as creators) stand together. Seeing the different creative disciplines converge makes me really happy, hence the motivation to write this article. The great thing is that young musical artists are increasingly displaying an understanding of the importance of art as part of their final product and this feature is playing a more prominent in the music-making process and life-cycle.

## Savanna Ruth Shares ‘Everything We Made’ from ‘The Baseball Diaries’


## Chicago singer-songwriter Savanna Ruth has shared ‘Everything We Made’, the latest track from ‘The Baseball Diaries’, her first album under the Savanna Ruth name, out October 23 via Easy Does It Records.
* * *
Savanna Ruth is the new chapter for Savanna Dickhut, who previously recorded as Burr Oak. After the more outward-looking storytelling of 2024’s ‘Annabelle’, ‘The Baseball Diaries’ turns back toward her own life, with songs written during the end of a long-term relationship and the changes that followed.
‘Everything We Made’ gets into the difficult part of looking back at a relationship that both people tried to save, even when the answer was already becoming clear. The music is bright and immediate, which makes the uncertainty underneath it hit a little harder.
“I didn’t want to make anyone the villain,” Ruth says. “I wanted to write from the perspective of someone (me or her) asking impossible questions, ‘Can we go back?’, while already knowing the answer.”
The song comes from Ruth’s experience of a relationship that became non-monogamous. She is careful not to treat that decision itself as the problem.
“I think some couples who decide to be in non-monogamous/polyamorous relationships do it successfully and it really works for them. It takes an extremely strong foundation of trust, rules and understanding. I think we genuinely wanted to try and do that in the beginning but it just was too hard, messy, and the relationship fell apart.”
For Ruth, what ultimately went wrong was simpler: both partners began falling for other people while their own relationship stopped getting the attention it needed.
Video 3
‘The Baseball Diaries’ follows Ruth through that period of upheaval, touching on attachment, desire and trying to work out who you are once a future you had taken for granted disappears. It follows ‘Bad Thoughts’, the first song shared from the record.
The album was produced by Scott Lucas of Local H and Blake Smith, with John Agnello handling the mix. Agnello’s long list of credits includes Dinosaur Jr., The Breeders and Redd Kross.
There is a nice contrast at the heart of ‘Everything We Made’. It doesn’t sound weighed down by everything Ruth is describing. Instead, the song moves quickly, while the lyrics are still circling the questions that tend to remain after something important ends.
* * *

#### by Jada E. Watson
One of the most overlooked songs of the last few years is RaeLynn’s “Love Triangle”. Widely applauded by critics and fans for its raw and emotional account of growing up the child of divorce, the song shockingly had limited impact on the charts. Released to radio on July 13, 2016 – three and a half years after writing the song – “Love Triangle” spent 30 weeks on the Hot Country Songs chart, and peaked at 27 two years ago today on April 15, 2017.
* * *
We first met RaeLynn in 2012 when she auditioned for the reality vocal competition show, _The Voice_, with her rendition of the Pistol Annies’ “Hell on Heels“.She proved to be a dynamic personality, a versatile performer, and a fierce champion of country music – performing Jason Aldean’s “She’s Country” and The Band Perry’s “If I Die Young”. Following her elimination from the show in the quarterfinal round, RaeLynn moved to Nashville, released her debut album, and toured with some of the genre’s most prominent artists. A Star Is Born is the soundtrack album to the 2018 musical film of the same name, performed by its stars Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper. It was released on October 5, 2018, by Interscope Records. Developed alongside the film's production, the soundtrack was conceived as a narrative-driven work, with songs written to reflect the characters' emotional arcs and function within the story. Cooper teamed up with Gaga's recurring collaborator DJ White Shadow and a range of musicians and songwriters, including Lukas Nelson, Jason Isbell, Mark Ronson, Diane Warren, and Andrew Wyatt. Much of the material was written during filming and evolved in tandem with the screenplay, as the production team shaped distinct musical identities for Cooper's Jackson Maine and Gaga's Ally.
Musically, the soundtrack is primarily a pop, pop rock and blues rock album, while also incorporating elements of country, folk rock, electropop, and dance-pop. Much of the music was created through a hybrid process that combined live vocals with pre-recorded instrumentation, helping recreate the atmosphere of the film. Its lyrics address love, change, personal struggle, and emotional vulnerability, while the sequencing follows the narrative progression from Jackson's rootsier material to Ally's more polished pop songs. The soundtrack was preceded by the lead single "Shallow", a major international hit, while "Always Remember Us This Way" and "I'll Never Love Again" were later released as singles in select countries.
The soundtrack received positive reviews from critics, who particularly praised Gaga's ballads, the chemistry between the two leads, and the way the music supports the film's narrative, though some felt the album was less effective outside the context of the film. It was also a major commercial success, topping charts in more than 20 countries and selling over six million copies worldwide. Among numerous accolades, "Shallow" won the Academy Award, Golden Globe Award, Critics' Choice Award, and two Grammy Awards, while the soundtrack won the Grammy Award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media and the BAFTA Award for Best Film Music.
Background and developmentedit

In March 2015, Warner Bros. announced that Bradley Cooper was in talks to make his directorial debut with A Star Is Born, the fourth iteration of the 1937 film of the same name.[1] Music supervisors Julia Michels and Julianne Jordan had sought to work on the project since an earlier incarnation involving Clint Eastwood and Beyoncé, and eventually joined Cooper's version.[2] American singer Lady Gaga was officially attached to the film in August 2016, with the studio green-lighting the project to begin production in early 2017.[3] Cooper decided to cast Gaga after seeing her perform Édith Piaf's "La Vie en rose" (1947) at a charity event, which he said "blew [him] away" and led him to envision her as Ally.[4] Gaga had performed the song for years before the film, and a rendition was later also recorded for the film and its soundtrack.[5] In A Star Is Born, Cooper plays Jackson Maine, an established country singer who discovers and falls in love with Ally, a struggling singer-songwriter, portrayed by Gaga in her first lead feature-film role.[6][7] Her rise to fame unfolds alongside his personal and professional decline, with Ally's success increasingly eclipsing Jackson’s fading career.[6][8]
Cooper spent two-and-a-half years prepping for the film and determining what kind of musician his character would be.[9] Gaga "helped inform Cooper's performance as a musician", advising him, "Work, and then you'll figure [it] out".[7][9] As part of the preparations, Cooper set up a six-month "boot camp" at his Los Angeles home, where he learned guitar and piano and trained his voice to sing like a seasoned professional.[4] He worked with vocal coach Roger Love and other musicians. Cooper said that, by the end of the process, Jackson "started developing into his own sort of creation"; if he had had another year of preparation, the character's music would have been "complete rock", but instead became "some sort of hybrid".[9]
Writing and recordingedit  
Jason Isbell wrote "Maybe It's Time" for Jackson Maine, which Bradley Cooper described as "the sword" from which much of the character's music emerged.

Cooper described the soundtrack "an evolution, like the story."[10] Gaga and Cooper were writing songs for the soundtrack during filming, with each track going through numerous iterations.[10] Cooper added that "the music really became a character in the movie. There is no lyric that's ever in any point of the movie that doesn't have exactly to do with where one of them is or hopes to be or regrets being. That was our launching pad and then it was just about discovering what songs fit in the right places."[10] Michels recalled hearing Gaga perform songs for the team at her kitchen table and described the early collaboration between Gaga and Cooper as "poignant, soulful and special". She and Jordan subsequently followed the songwriting process, observing how Gaga wrote and selected collaborators and how Cooper developed his own material; Michels said the songs and story continually informed one another.[2] Changes to the film's script also influenced the music; for example, "Shallow" was initially conceived as a solo song by Ally for the end credits, when the story ended with Jackson dying by drowning—an idea that informed the song's imagery—before it was reworked into a central love song between the film's protagonists.[11][12]

A Star Is Born is the soundtrack album to the 2018 musical film of the same name, performed by its stars Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper. It was released on October 5, 2018, by Interscope Records. Developed alongside the film's production, the soundtrack was conceived as a narrative-driven work, with songs written to reflect the characters' emotional arcs and function within the story. Cooper teamed up with Gaga's recurring collaborator DJ White Shadow and a range of musicians and songwriters, including Lukas Nelson, Jason Isbell, Mark Ronson, Diane Warren, and Andrew Wyatt. Much of the material was written during filming and evolved in tandem with the screenplay, as the production team shaped distinct musical identities for Cooper's Jackson Maine and Gaga's Ally.
Musically, the soundtrack is primarily a pop, pop rock and blues rock album, while also incorporating elements of country, folk rock, electropop, and dance-pop. Much of the music was created through a hybrid process that combined live vocals with pre-recorded instrumentation, helping recreate the atmosphere of the film. Its lyrics address love, change, personal struggle, and emotional vulnerability, while the sequencing follows the narrative progression from Jackson's rootsier material to Ally's more polished pop songs. The soundtrack was preceded by the lead single "Shallow", a major international hit, while "Always Remember Us This Way" and "I'll Never Love Again" were later released as singles in select countries.
The soundtrack received positive reviews from critics, who particularly praised Gaga's ballads, the chemistry between the two leads, and the way the music supports the film's narrative, though some felt the album was less effective outside the context of the film. It was also a major commercial success, topping charts in more than 20 countries and selling over six million copies worldwide. Among numerous accolades, "Shallow" won the Academy Award, Golden Globe Award, Critics' Choice Award, and two Grammy Awards, while the soundtrack won the Grammy Award for Best Compilation Soundtrack for Visual Media and the BAFTA Award for Best Film Music.
Background and developmentedit
texts.2:
In March 2015, Warner Bros. announced that Bradley Cooper was in talks to make his directorial debut with A Star Is Born, the fourth iteration of the 1937 film of the same name.[1] Music supervisors Julia Michels and Julianne Jordan had sought to work on the project since an earlier incarnation involving Clint Eastwood and Beyoncé, and eventually joined Cooper's version.[2] American singer Lady Gaga was officially attached to the film in August 2016, with the studio green-lighting the project to begin production in early 2017.[3] Cooper decided to cast Gaga after seeing her perform Édith Piaf's "La Vie en rose" (1947) at a charity event, which he said "blew [him] away" and led him to envision her as Ally.[4] Gaga had performed the song for years before the film, and a rendition was later also recorded for the film and its soundtrack.[5] In A Star Is Born, Cooper plays Jackson Maine, an established country singer who discovers and falls in love with Ally, a struggling singer-songwriter, portrayed by Gaga in her first lead feature-film role.[6][7] Her rise to fame unfolds alongside his personal and professional decline, with Ally's success increasingly eclipsing Jackson’s fading career.[6][8]
Cooper spent two-and-a-half years prepping for the film and determining what kind of musician his character would be.[9] Gaga "helped inform Cooper's performance as a musician", advising him, "Work, and then you'll figure [it] out".[7][9] As part of the preparations, Cooper set up a six-month "boot camp" at his Los Angeles home, where he learned guitar and piano and trained his voice to sing like a seasoned professional.[4] He worked with vocal coach Roger Love and other musicians. Cooper said that, by the end of the process, Jackson "started developing into his own sort of creation"; if he had had another year of preparation, the character's music would have been "complete rock", but instead became "some sort of hybrid".[9]
Writing and recordingedit  
Jason Isbell wrote "Maybe It's Time" for Jackson Maine, which Bradley Cooper described as "the sword" from which much of the character's music emerged.
texts.3: Cooper described the soundtrack "an evolution, like the story."[10] Gaga and Cooper were writing songs for the soundtrack during filming, with each track going through numerous iterations.[10] Cooper added that "the music really became a character in the movie. There is no lyric that's ever in any point of the movie that doesn't have exactly to do with where one of them is or hopes to be or regrets being. That was our launching pad and then it was just about discovering what songs fit in the right places."[10] Michels recalled hearing Gaga perform songs for the team at her kitchen table and described the early collaboration between Gaga and Cooper as "poignant, soulful and special". She and Jordan subsequently followed the songwriting process, observing how Gaga wrote and selected collaborators and how Cooper developed his own material; Michels said the songs and story continually informed one another.[2] Changes to the film's script also influenced the music; for example, "Shallow" was initially conceived as a solo song by Ally for the end credits, when the story ended with Jackson dying by drowning—an idea that informed the song's imagery—before it was reworked into a central love song between the film's protagonists.[11][12]

## corook Tries “BDSM” In Her Newest Single About Long-Term Relationships
After her debut festival appearance at Bonaroo, corook (a self-described “singer, songwriter, producer, multi-instrumentalist, and huge f*ckin dork”) dropped her newest single, “BDSM.” The track is full of corook’s light, airy vocals, along with a mixture of electric and acoustic guitar that builds up to the chorus’ climax which brings in the drum pad. Sprinkled throughout the song are cool electronic sounds and vocal effects that create a fun composition with a unique twist.
The song is inspired by her long-term relationship with her girlfriend, Olivia, and as corook goes on to explain,
> “_I didn’t think I wanted to write love songs_. _I feel like love songs are usually cheesy and hard to listen to because they’re always just rainbows and butterflies. I realized the best part about my relationship is that I can tell my partner anything. I can tell her when I’m not really feeling it, or when I need something different, or when I’m not excited, and neither of us take it as a threat to our relationship. It’s just the truth. I’m really grateful for someone I can be that honest with. Relationships naturally get more predictable, and things can get boring, but when you stick it out, that love gets deeper and safer and way juicier. This is a realistic love song for all the people in long-term relationships._”
corook and her girlfriend Olivia (Photo Credit: Christina Coleman)
“BDSM” showcases corook’s unique musical style, where she delves into deeply personal themes through a quirky and humorous lens. In the case of this specific single, corook uses BDSM as an example of how it can be fun to spice up a long-term relationship, especially after spending time getting to know each other. This is exemplified in the chorus, “Baby, I’m bored, we should explore/ We could try BDSM, you can tie my hands to the headboard/ Wait, I take it back, that’s really not me/ We just need some spice, if you know what I mean,” along with lyrics like, “But sometimes, I wish that we could turn time back/ Kiss you for the first time, for the first time again/ And happily choose to be bored all over again.”

## corook Tries “BDSM” In Her Newest Single About Long-Term Relationships
If you like “BDSM,” then listen to corook’s debut EP _achoo!_ which features popular singles such as the fan favorite, “snakes.” Also, be sure to follow corook on Instagram and Tiktok or check out her official website at corook.com to stay up to date on her music.
For now, be sure to give “BDSM” a listen!

* * *
**Local Nomad**dive into what happens in a relationship when the love is gone in their latest track, "Love is Gone." The single carries many of the band's signature sounds including, Michael Desmond's warm and soulful vocals, dream-like synths, and glossy drum beats that manage to keep you grounded. Throughout the song, we hear about what happens when a long term relationship ends suddenly and feelings of pain, adaptation and freedom that come with it. According to Desmond, he wrote "Love is Gone" after his six-year relationship ended over a phone call and wanted the track to be harsh, funny, and authentic. These feelings are incredibly evident throughout the piece, but especially so in the song's final chorus as Desmond emotionally sings the lyrics, "No, I don't know you anymore, my chameleon girl. You're changing your mind all of the time...you think I'm color blind."
— Alessandra Rincon on February 21, 2020
* * *
After the passing of her dear friend, Pam,**Jocelyn Mackenzie** sought out to write a song to Pam's grieving husband."Love Begets Love" is the beautiful product of Mackenzie's efforts, a song about the consistent readiness and availability of love.As if an echo of Pam's heart, Mackenzie spreads a personal and universal message about how love can grow and foster in the midst of hardships. Mackenzie's voice has healing elements in and of itself, but it reaches to new levels when accompanied by the colorful background vocals which in a way sound like a united band of caring friends reaching out to a loved one in a time of need.While the pain of loss will never be truly erased, this song is a reminder that there truly is consolation and hope in love. "Love Begets Love" is featured on a compilation album dedicated to Pam's memory called _Songs for Pam_ which can be found on Burst and Bloom Records's bandcamp. New Yorkers, be sure to see **Jocelyn Mackenzie**during her residency at C'mon Everybody in Brooklyn on August 11, September 16, and October 13!
— Dara Bankole on August 6, 2018
* * *

**Wild Pink’s** “Lake Erie” is full of all sorts of meaningfully mundane details one has no choice but to notice while growing up in a small town. “Your body looks impossibly small when you hang your head and cry / Meanwhile people on Tumblr unpack neuroses,” singer John Ross observes. He is unable to shake the tiny details once so familiar to him — a particular intersection or the smell on a rainy day. It is as much a song about leaving as it is a song about home. “You thought you’d never get out,” Ross reminisces in the chorus before finally flipping to the first person to marvel at his own growth. The song has an Americana sound tied more to the road than to any particular place. A wistful pedal steel guitar pines over the old days on top of a rhythm section as unrelentingly steady as the passage of time, declaring that there is no going back.
— Daniel Shanker on August 6, 2018
* * *
Although **Lucy Dacus** believes Richmond band **Spooky Cool** should be renamed “Stupid Good,” the band currently has the perfect name to describe their haunting indie pop vibe. The newest single “Old Hair Mine” off their upcoming debut EP “Every Thing Ever” is full of nostalgic lyrics and vocal harmonies mixed with the instrumentations dis-harmonization and a constantly changing rhythmic backdrop. The product is an entertaining, intricate piece that feels timeless and futuristic.At the end of the song, the vocalists question over and over again “is anything real?” Not sure about that, but we'll keep wondering as we listen to this song.
— Kathryn Brooks on August 2, 2018
* * *

With a highly anticipated new record on the way,**Odetta Hartman**releases her last single off of the album _\_.**"**\__ You You" is the epitome of short and sweet,showcasing Hartman in all her old school charm but with a feel-good twist. While an**Odetta Hartman**track is usually embedded with experimental and genre-bending sounds, "You You" finds its strength in its sweet simplicity. Opening up with a hard-hitting electric guitar, Hartman's voice is a contrast of sorts with it's quiet strength and colorful timbre which remains the centerpiece of the song. "You You" is the kind of love song that doesn't feel crowded with frivolous emotions but rather heart and soul. "I want to run / to edge of the earth with you / it's perfect with you," Hartman repeats in the chorus, giving us a glimpse of her desire for an adventurous romance thats more about togetherness and less about the frills.Catch _Old Rockhounds Never Die_ out on August 10!
— Dara Bankole on August 1, 2018
* * *

**Local Nomad**dive into what happens in a relationship when the love is gone in their latest track, "Love is Gone." The single carries many of the band's signature sounds including, Michael Desmond's warm and soulful vocals, dream-like synths, and glossy drum beats that manage to keep you grounded. Throughout the song, we hear about what happens when a long term relationship ends suddenly and feelings of pain, adaptation and freedom that come with it. According to Desmond, he wrote "Love is Gone" after his six-year relationship ended over a phone call and wanted the track to be harsh, funny, and authentic. These feelings are incredibly evident throughout the piece, but especially so in the song's final chorus as Desmond emotionally sings the lyrics, "No, I don't know you anymore, my chameleon girl. Mackenzie's voice has healing elements in and of itself, but it reaches to new levels when accompanied by the colorful background vocals which in a way sound like a united band of caring friends reaching out to a loved one in a time of need.While the pain of loss will never be truly erased, this song is a reminder that there truly is consolation and hope in love. "Love Begets Love" is featured on a compilation album dedicated to Pam's memory called _Songs for Pam_ which can be found on Burst and Bloom Records's bandcamp. New Yorkers, be sure to see **Jocelyn Mackenzie**during her residency at C'mon Everybody in Brooklyn on August 11, September 16, and October 13!

He is unable to shake the tiny details once so familiar to him — a particular intersection or the smell on a rainy day. The song has an Americana sound tied more to the road than to any particular place. A wistful pedal steel guitar pines over the old days on top of a rhythm section as unrelentingly steady as the passage of time, declaring that there is no going back.

## corook Tries “BDSM” In Her Newest Single About Long-Term Relationships
After her debut festival appearance at Bonaroo, corook (a self-described “singer, songwriter, producer, multi-instrumentalist, and huge f*ckin dork”) dropped her newest single, “BDSM.” The track is full of corook’s light, airy vocals, along with a mixture of electric and acoustic guitar that builds up to the chorus’ climax which brings in the drum pad. Sprinkled throughout the song are cool electronic sounds and vocal effects that create a fun composition with a unique twist.
The song is inspired by her long-term relationship with her girlfriend, Olivia, and as corook goes on to explain,
> “_I didn’t think I wanted to write love songs_. _I feel like love songs are usually cheesy and hard to listen to because they’re always just rainbows and butterflies. I realized the best part about my relationship is that I can tell my partner anything. I can tell her when I’m not really feeling it, or when I need something different, or when I’m not excited, and neither of us take it as a threat to our relationship. It’s just the truth. I’m really grateful for someone I can be that honest with. Relationships naturally get more predictable, and things can get boring, but when you stick it out, that love gets deeper and safer and way juicier. This is a realistic love song for all the people in long-term relationships._”
corook and her girlfriend Olivia (Photo Credit: Christina Coleman)
“BDSM” showcases corook’s unique musical style, where she delves into deeply personal themes through a quirky and humorous lens. In the case of this specific single, corook uses BDSM as an example of how it can be fun to spice up a long-term relationship, especially after spending time getting to know each other. This is exemplified in the chorus, “Baby, I’m bored, we should explore/ We could try BDSM, you can tie my hands to the headboard/ Wait, I take it back, that’s really not me/ We just need some spice, if you know what I mean,” along with lyrics like, “But sometimes, I wish that we could turn time back/ Kiss you for the first time, for the first time again/ And happily choose to be bored all over again.”
